items.title: Frontier AI for DevOps workflows
items.hook: Turning DevOps workflows into AI skills and evals grounded in real practice
items.role: Led research end to end, from discovery to validation. Partnered with a product manager, a designer and a data scientist.

why.frame: In AI chat, the response is the experience. People don't work in one app. Their work runs across an ecosystem of tools, so AI only helps if it understands the workflow around the question.
why.insight: AI is increasing output and delivery pressure, but human systems are not absorbing either cleanly.
why.quote: The development time is already being short enough with the help of LLM models. But the other things, which are integration with different teams, the dependencies with different teams, these still remain the same.

phases.name: Understanding the domain and the users
Scenario deep dives
outcomes: User mental models → evals and assertions
46 evalsets with assertions grounded in end-user workflows, improving core Copilot quality.
6 new skills across enterprise connectors for the DevOps domain, now in internal dogfood.

judgmentCalls.label: Recruiting
judgmentCalls.text: Advanced skill users were scarce and needed vendor support. I **repivoted the foundational study to workflows**, which still shaped the product.
judgmentCalls.learning: Vendor support earlier could have changed the sequence of the study.

judgmentCalls.label: Engagement
judgmentCalls.text: The planned diary study drew little engagement. With a product manager and a data scientist, I **built the skills and a prototype with AI instead**.
judgmentCalls.learning: A diary study could have given more depth, but this approach got us out sooner and fed learning into the next research phase.

judgmentCalls.label: Realism
judgmentCalls.text: Validation needed more than a fixed-path prototype, and prototypes can't be deployed into customer environments. With the same partners, I **built a tool and a synthetic-data environment** close to real deployment, and validated with real users.
judgmentCalls.learning: How testing of AI products is shifting, and what becomes possible when prototypes are built close to real rather than on fixed paths.

items.title: Craft Evaluator
items.hook: Scaling UX craft evaluation with AI, without losing human judgment

why.frame: As products grow more complex, it gets harder to consistently catch UX regressions. This work shows how AI can evaluate user jobs at scale, while human judgment stays central to decision making.
why.insight: Craft needs to scale. Quality must be repeatable, not heroic.

list: Issues caught continuously, so regressions don't slip through.
Craft applied across journeys, not one-off reviews.

items.title: Synthetic Users
items.hook: Testing where synthetic users hold up in research, and where they break

why.frame: I started with a lot of uncertainty, fear and mixed emotions. So I approached it like a researcher: with curiosity, and by looking inward at my own biases. Then I set it up as an experiment.
why.insight: Can synthetic users replace real users for research studies?

sections.title: The experiment
paragraphs: Six variations of a contact card were shown to both synthetic and real users. Each variation showed attributes (name, profile picture, contact information) that were similar or different between two contacts, and the task was to identify duplicates.
Synthetic users came from a custom GPT set up to play a participant in a user interview, and fed transcript data to internalize the role. Three rounds, with both text and image input.

cards.label: Question 1
cards.text: Is the contact a duplicate or not?

cards.label: Question 2
cards.text: Should the system handle this, or should it be handled manually?

cards.label: Question 3
cards.text: Should the contacts be linked or merged?

visuals.alt: The six contact card variations shown to participants
visuals.caption: The six contact card variations

sections.title: What we saw
paragraphs: Synthetic users gave different answers from real users in **all six scenarios**. The gap was starkest in the most complex one, scenario 6.

visuals.alt: Responses by case, with shaded cells where synthetic users differed from real users
visuals.caption: Responses by case. Shaded cells mark where synthetic answers differed from real users.

cards.label: Inconsistent rationale
cards.text: Real users who are risk averse stay risk averse across scenarios. Synthetic users don't, unless that behavior is explicitly scripted.

cards.label: Logical, but fixed
cards.text: Synthetic users articulated reasoning for most cases, but it was scenario-bound and static. Real users adapted to context: they merged contacts with differing profile images when other attributes aligned, and merged identical pictures despite other differences. Synthetic reasoning counted matching criteria, not the confidence in each.

cards.label: The human layer is missing
cards.text: Synthetic responses were linear. Human responses draw on vast experience and an underlying need or pain.

sections.title: My point of view
sections.callout: A synthetic user is not going to replace real user feedback.
paragraphs: It can help build better hypotheses when abstracted to a persona level, improve the algorithm, and help refine questions after a pilot.

sections.title: Impact
list: Challenged an existing belief about synthetic users and helped the team understand the current state.
Enabled the team to reflect on and re-look at synthetic users.
AI experiment champion in the research community, with the opportunity to present AI topics at UXR Day talks in consecutive years.

items.title: Copilot Dash
items.hook: A playground for on-device AI: small models on your phone, private and offline

homeImage.alt: Copilot Dash hackathon page showing the app on a phone

why.frame: A hack for low-cost AI. Small language models offer security, privacy and easy access to AI, and there are **5.7 billion mobile devices** worldwide. Dash puts a capable model right on the phone, no signal needed.

sections.title: What it is
paragraphs: A playground for on-device AI. Explore small language models, chat with the model of your choice, use ready-made apps powered by them, or describe a skill and build your own.

visuals.alt: Copilot Dash home screen on a phone
visuals.caption: Copilot Dash home screen

cards.label: Choose your model
cards.text: Browse the model catalog, pick the best small language model for your device, and download it once.

cards.label: Chat, privately
cards.text: Chat with the model of your choice. Conversations stay on the device.

cards.label: Ready-made apps
cards.text: Task-focused apps for everyday things like taking notes and studying.

cards.label: Dash Builder
cards.text: Create your own AI-native apps just by describing what you want.

cards.label: Offline travel
cards.text: Mid-flight with no internet, Dash plans an itinerary and answers travel questions, completely offline.

cards.label: Neighborhood shop
cards.text: A finance hub reads transaction SMS, tracks income and expenses, and generates spending insights, all from SMS data.

cards.label: Study
cards.text: A fifth-grade student in rural India turns textbook chapters into notes and quizzes.

sections.title: Under the hood
paragraphs: A native Android app with a shared on-device inference layer and dedicated pipelines for speech, image and text.
